paper_title: Can We Edit LLMs for Long-Tail Biomedical Knowledge
caption: : The performance on BioGPT.
model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC %) of six different methods—Base, FT, IKE, MEND, MEMIT, and ROME—on the BioGPT model as a function of the co-occurrence number, which is plotted on a logarithmic x-axis ranging from 0 to approximately 10⁴. The y-axis represents accuracy in percentage, ranging from 30% to 55%, with major gridlines at 5% intervals. The “Base” method (black line with circular markers) remains nearly flat, starting at ~28.5% and ending at ~32%. The “FT” method (blue line with downward-pointing triangular markers) increases gradually from ~32% to ~38.5%. The “IKE” method (red line with upward-pointing triangular markers) shows a steady rise from ~32.5% to ~41.5%. The “MEND” method (brown line with diamond markers) starts at ~36.5%, rises to ~45% at 10², and plateaus near 45.5%. The “MEMIT” method (purple line with pentagonal markers) begins at ~36%, climbs to ~43.5% at 10², and stabilizes around 46.5%. The “ROME” method (green line with square markers) exhibits the steepest growth, starting at ~43.5% and rising to ~58.5% at the highest co-occurrence number. All lines are solid, and the legend is positioned in the top-left corner.
